item.title: Interlay and Kintsugi Restart Runbook
item.dc:creator: Dominik Harz
item.content:encoded:
With the restart runbook, anyone can fully restart the Interlay and Kintsugi chains.

Prerequisites:

DOT (Interlay) or KSM (Kintsugi) to buy coretime.

To be published:

  • Collator session keys: In progress

Chain data snapshots:

Interlay snapshot:
https://snapshots.interlay.io/snapshots/interlay-archive-10885373.tar.zst
Checksum: https://snapshots.interlay.io/snapshots/interlay-archive-10885373.tar.zst.sha256

Kintsugi snapshot:
https://snapshots.interlay.io/snapshots/kintsugi-archive-9762082.tar.zst
Checksum: https://snapshots.interlay.io/snapshots/kintsugi-archive-9762082.tar.zst.sha256

Node software:

  • interbtc (https://github.com/interlay/interbtc)
  • Chain specs: https://github.com/interlay/interbtc/tree/master/parachain/res

Step 1. Acquire Coretime

On the Coretime chain, call broker.purchaseduring a sale, then broker.assign(region,paraId,Final). Cost is the market sale price.

Interlay paraId is 2032. Kintsugi paraId is 2092.

The paraId stays registered after the halt. Head state and validation code are retained, so no re-registration is needed.

Step 2. Start Collators

Code: https://github.com/interlay/interbtc

  1. Download the pruned or archived chain state snapshot. Note: best to work from the archive for full history.
  2. Run the interbtc node as a collator with the published chain state and Aura session keys. Setup guide: https://docs.interlay.io/#/collator/guide.
  3. Collator keys are published as a GitHub gist at halt. Sync the database to the last finalized block from the published snapshot.

Once a core is scheduled, collators author blocks and relay validators include them.

After step 2, blocks should be produced again. Governance, token transfers, and other core functions are reactivated.

Step 3. Restart Off-Chain Services

Code: https://github.com/interlay/interbtc-clients (clients), UI (https://github.com/interlay/interbtc-ui), Indexing (https://github.com/interlay/interbtc-squid)

  1. Vault client, which also submits Bitcoin block headers (permissionless): https://github.com/interlay/interbtc-clients/blob/master/vault/README.md. Register with collateral to serve issue and redeem.
  2. Oracle client: https://github.com/interlay/interbtc-clients/blob/master/oracle/README.md. Cannot feed until its account is authorized by governance (Step 4). Until then, exchange rates stay stale and issue and redeem are blocked.
  3. Indexer and UI: start the Indexer (https://github.com/interlay/interbtc-squid) to ensure the UI works. Then run the interbtc-ui (https://github.com/interlay/interbtc-ui) against the new RPC endpoint.

After step 3, the iBTC/kBTC bridges are reactivated pending the oracle activation.

Step 4. Use Governance to Authorize Services and Rotate Keys.

Governance is live and community-controlled. No sudo key exists; Democracy referenda (voted with locked native tokens, vINTR and vKINT) dispatch as Root. Existing token holders pass referenda to:

  1. Authorize new oracle accounts ( oracle.insert_authrozied_oracle), remove the old ones. Fresh exchange-rate feeds unblock issue and redeem.
  2. Replace technical committee membership.
  3. Register fresh collators (operators call session.set_keys, then collatorSelection.set_invulnerables). The published bootstrap keys become inert.
  4. Optionally, on Interlay only: Adopt Kintsugi collator-selection to reduce DoS exposure/allow community collators to join.

After step 4, the chains are fully restored.

Chain Data Snapshots

IMPORTANT: If the chains are shut down again after restarting them, take snapshots and publish them.

A revived parachain must continue from the last block (the relay chain tracks the existing head, so genesis cannot be reset), so a node needs the chain database to reach that head. Once the Interlay/Kintsugi nodes shut down, there are no peers to sync from, so the database must be published as a static download.

Both chains’ collators run RocksDB with — pruning=archive (node 1.25.4, polkadot-sdk v1.0.0). The relay-chain database is not part of the snapshot; revivers use relay-chain-rpc-urls. We need one type of snapshot:

Full archive: the complete chains/<network>/db/full directory. Needed so the indexer, UI, and historians can rebuild the full history. Without it, historical data is unrecoverable.

Steps to create the snapshot on production:

  1. Stop the collator for a consistent copy, at or after halt.
  2. Tar and compress the parachain db:
tar -C <base-path>/chains/<network> -cf - db/full | zstd -3 > snapshot.tar.zst

3. Upload to object storage or IPFS.

Restore (reviver): extract into <base-path>/chains/<network>/db/full and start the node with the default RocksDB backend.

item.title: Closing a Chapter: Winding Down Interlay and Kintsugi
item.dc:creator: Dominik Harz
item.content:encoded:
Today, we are announcing the orderly wind-down of the Interlay and Kintsugi networks.

What you need to do

If you hold assets on Interlay or Kintsugi, withdraw your external assets before 22 July 2026.

  • External assets can be withdrawn. Your Bitcoin (held as iBTC or kBTC) and any assets bridged from other chains (for example, DOT, USDT, USDC, KSM, vDOT, LKSM). Withdraw all of these before the deadline.
  • INTR and KINT cannot be withdrawn. They are the native tokens of the chains. They cannot be unstaked and moved off, bridged, or transferred to another network. This includes staked and vote-locked (escrow) balances. They stay on their chain.

After 22 July 2026, the chains stop producing blocks, and all remaining funds are locked on the chain. The shutdown will be completed so that the community can restart the network should it wish to do so, following comprehensive instructions we will provide.

Where we came from

This began as an academic problem. Alexei and Dom met during their PhDs, working on research into trustless cross-chain bridges that would ultimately become XCLAIM. In 2019, the Web3 Foundation approached them to turn that research into something real: a Bitcoin bridge for Polkadot. We have been building on that idea ever since.

The bridge started life as PolkaBTC, conceived as a public good for the ecosystem, a trustless way to bring Bitcoin to Polkadot, owned by no one and available to all. When it became clear that the Kusama DAO would not support public-good status, we turned the work into a project in its own right. Interlay was born as the main network and Kintsugi as its canary version. On both Kusama and Polkadot, we competed in the earliest parachain auctions and brought Interlay and Kintsugi live in the second batches of parachains ever to launch on the networks.

From a research paper to two live networks securing real Bitcoin, it has been a long road, and one we are proud of.

What we built

We set out to do something much of the industry said could not be done trustlessly: bring Bitcoin into DeFi without a custodian, without an IOU you had to trust, and without a single point of failure.

interBTC was, to our knowledge, the first genuinely trustless and decentralized Bitcoin bridge ever built. Based on the XCLAIM framework, it let anyone mint iBTC on Interlay and kBTC on Kintsugi, backed 1:1 by real Bitcoin and secured by a permissionless network of over-collateralized vaults rather than by centralized operators holding your keys. Around it we built a full Bitcoin DeFi hub, with an AMM and a money market, and the plumbing to move BTC across the multi-chain world. We are proud of the engineering, and the code has been open source from day one.

What we contributed to the wider ecosystem

We always tried to invest beyond our own four walls:

  • We coordinated the Banxa on-ramp grant that brought fiat access to a range of parachains, not only our own.
  • We helped spin the business-development arm of Parity out into Velocity Labs to make the broader ecosystem more ready to go to market.
  • We helped bootstrap the Polkadot Assurance Legion (PAL), which coordinated funding from the Polkadot DAO to pay for security audits across ecosystem projects, helping safeguard them from hacks.

Why we are winding down

We will be straight with you. Interlay and Kintsugi have been in maintenance mode for some time. We have not shipped meaningful protocol updates in roughly two years, and the networks have been quietly running rather than growing. Bitcoin DeFi in the Polkadot ecosystem did not reach the scale it needed to sustain active development, and our energy has moved to where that same vision is now finding traction.

Keeping two networks running indefinitely with no active development serves no one. The honest and responsible step is to formally wind them down now, in the open, while the bridge still works and while everyone can still withdraw their funds.

How we are leaving

We are leaving with our heads held high. We gave this our best for years, far beyond what Interlay alone ever required of us. We have nothing to hide, and we believe this is simply the right thing to do.

The networks do not disappear

Interlay and Kintsugi are not being switched off and deleted. Every line of code is open source, governance has always lived on-chain in the hands of the community, and we are publishing everything needed to restart the networks: full chain snapshots, the collator keys, and a step-by-step revival runbook. If the community wishes to carry these chains forward, the door is open.

The mission continues

We still believe Bitcoin should be the foundation of an open financial system, not an asset sitting on the sidelines. That is exactly what we are now building with BOB, where Bitcoin DeFi is finding the audience and the traction we always wanted for it. The Interlay chapter is closing. The mission stays.

A personal note

To everyone who minted an iBTC, ran a vault, wrote a proposal, filed a bug, or simply believed in trustless Bitcoin finance when it was an unfashionable thing to believe in: thank you. You took a bet on a hard idea and a small team, and you stayed. We are proud of what we built together, and we hope you will come and see what we are building next.
To our community, our vault operators, our partners across the ecosystem, and everyone who contributed: thank you. It has been a genuine privilege.
– The Interlay team

Frequently asked questions

Can I withdraw my INTR or KINT?

No. INTR and KINT are the native tokens of the chains and cannot be withdrawn, unstaked-and-moved-off, bridged, or transferred to another network. This includes any staked or vote-locked (escrow) balances. They remain on their respective chain.

Which assets can I withdraw, then?

Everything that is not native: your Bitcoin held as iBTC and kBTC, and any assets bridged in from other chains (for example DOT, USDT, USDC, KSM, vDOT, LKSM). Withdraw all of these before the deadline.

I hold iBTC or kBTC. How do I get my Bitcoin back?

Redeem them for BTC in the app, where vaults stay online until the deadline to fulfil redemptions. Note that a large portion of iBTC and kBTC has already been liquidated. Those amounts cannot be redeemed for BTC and must instead be burned for the underlying collateral (for example DOT or KSM) in the app. The app will guide you to whichever path applies to your holdings.

What is the deadline?

22 July 2026.

What if I miss the deadline?

Once coretime expires, the chains stop producing blocks and all remaining funds are locked on the chain. They could only be accessed again if the community restarts the network using the published runbook. For external assets bridged from other chains (such as DOT, KSM, or vDOT), the governance of those other chains can also decide to unlock the corresponding assets on their side of the XCM channel.

What happens to my INTR or KINT after the shutdown?

They stay on the chain. INTR and KINT are already delisted from exchanges, so there is no route to sell or move them off-chain. They remain on their network and, if the community revives it, keep their on-chain and governance role.

Will the app and bridge stay online until then?

Yes. The app, the bridge, the vaults, the price feeds, and the cross-chain channels all stay live until the deadline.

What about the Interlay and Kintsugi DAO assets?

Any external assets held by the Interlay and Kintsugi DAO will remain on the chain and can be used by the community to fund the network in the future, should this be the desired outcome.

item.title: March 2024 Ecosystem Update
item.dc:creator: Interlay
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to Interlay’s Ecosystem Update for March 2024!

We’ve crushed milestones and we are thrilled to share the exciting progress at Interlay last month. As a key player in the decentralized ecosystem, our mission has always been to foster innovation, scalability, and interoperability on Bitcoin.

TVL Updates

As the Defi ecosystem adopts Bitcoin, the Total Value Locked (TVL) on Interlay has been on the rise with a recorded TVL ATH of 21.66 Million USD last month.

Currently sitting at 11.46 Million USD (excluding borrows) and Over 2x since its ATH of last year, It is evident that the Bitcoin takeover is near.

You can track the TVL on Interlay here:https://defillama.com/chain/Interlay

Governance Updates

Interlay Referendum #94

To bring more liquidity into the Interlay lending market, a proposal to register HDX token on the Interlay chain has been executed.

This Proposal will add HDX to the Interlay DEX, create a money market for lending and borrowing HDX, and capture possible fees from borrowing and lending HDX tokens

For more details check out:
https://interlay.subsquare.io/democracy/referenda/95

Interlay Proposal #100

A proposal to Adjust USDT and USDC lending market parameters on Interlay was tabled.

This proposal will adjust the lending jump curve for both the USDT and USDC markets and increase the market cap of $USDT to $2 million and the liquidation threshold for USDT to 87% to match USDC.

Read more here: https://interlay.subsquare.io/democracy/proposals/100

Events

Interlay Community Call

On the 3rd of March 2024, we had a usual community call where our co-founder Alexie joined us to discuss “the Path forward” for Interlay.

The Technical roadmap which includes adding new lending markets and vault collaterals to increase diversity was discussed.

Find out more about our Business development initiatives and other important discussions on the call here: https://interlay.medium.com/interlay-the-path-forward-5695a5515a0c

Integrations

Interlay Live on Dune

Being the leading Bitcoin DeFi provider in the Polkadot ecosystem, Interlay was listed as one of the first six Polkadot and Kusama parachains to go live on Dune Analytics.

With this integration, users and the general Polkadot community can seamlessly track Interlay on-chain activities in real-time.

Track here: https://dune.com/substrate/interlay

See the announcement here: https://x.com/InterlayHQ/status/1770550574548988043?s=20

$iBTC<> $DOT Pool Live on Stellaswap

Interlays $iBTC won the latest Stellaswap Vote-For-Boost and and by a large margin too.

We are grateful to our solid community for rallying behind us to achive this feat.

The $iBTC<>$DOT pool is live on stellaswap and now incentivized.

Check out the announcement here: https://x.com/InterlayHQ/status/1770550574548988043?s=https://x.com/InterlayHQ/status/1770467056590225626?s=20

Interlay X $VARCH

Last month, we collaborated with Invarch to reward active users who utilized $VDOT or $DOT on Interlay. They were airdropped a chunk of the 40,000,000 $VARCH tokens.

See the announcement here: https://x.com/InterlayHQ/status/1765728342211190942?s=20

Interlay X $PINK

Oh! There’s more…

$VDOT holders on Interlay at Block Height 4542124 also got airdropped an allocation of the +25, 000,000 $PINK tokens distributed by the Bitfrost team.

See the announcement here: https://x.com/InterlayHQ/status/1772651514512789764?s=20

Community

Last month the community voted on some important Governance matters.

Interlay In the Media

That’s it from March, see you next month!

About Interlay

Interlay is the global layer for all things Bitcoin finance. BTC trading, lending, staking, and a way to deploy into other DeFi products. Trustless bridge at the core, AMM and money market on top, wrapped in a simple one-click interface with on/off-ramps and multi-chain support.

Follow both Interlay and Kintsugi on Twitter, join our Telegram, and hop in our Discord to keep up to date with daily updates from the team.

INTR token on CoinMarketCap

Last month INTR, KINT & iBTC, kBTC got featured under different categories on CoinGecko!

We are pleased to announce that now they are now featured on Coinmarketcap also.

Also, kBTC and iBTC are now featured under wrapped tokens.

INTR on HydraDX omnipool

INTR is now live for trading on HydraDX’s omnipool with good liquidity to support small to large swaps.

iBTC is now available to trade on Polkadex Orderbook. You can now trade non-custodial limit & market orders for the best decentralized version of Bitcoin.

Decentralized BTC 🤝 Decentralized Exchange

Here are some interesting pieces that we put out this month that will help you give a context on the things we are working on.

item.content:encoded:
We are thrilled to share the exciting progress at Interlay last month. As a key player in the decentralized ecosystem, our mission has always been to foster innovation, scalability, and interoperability on Bitcoin.

General Updates

CoinGecko Feature

INTR, KINT, iBTC & kBTC are now featured under different categories on CoinGecko, the popular crypto data aggregator. Most notably INTR/KINT are now listed under:

  • Bridge governance token: https://www.coingecko.com/en/categories/bridge-governance-tokens
  • Polkadot Ecosystem: https://www.coingecko.com/en/categories/dot-ecosystem
  • DEX tokens: https://www.coingecko.com/en/categories/decentralized-exchange
  • L1 tokens: https://www.coingecko.com/en/categories/layer-1

Also, kBTC and iBTC are now featured under wrapped tokens quite prominently.

BOB Alpha Testnet is now live!

The First BOB Alpha on Testnet is now LIVE!

  • Bitcoin smart contracts
  • BTC Light Client
  • Trustless P2P swap BTC <> ERC20 tokens

Check out this thread to know more 👇

BOB | Build On Bitcoin on Twitter: "Building on Bitcoin just got easier. 🧡Bitcoin EVM interaction is here. 🌉Introducing the First BOB Alpha Testnet!Here's a 🧵 breaking down the various ALPHA live on testnet👇 pic.twitter.com/JiUDQUnuLt / Twitter"

Building on Bitcoin just got easier. 🧡Bitcoin EVM interaction is here. 🌉Introducing the First BOB Alpha Testnet!Here's a 🧵 breaking down the various ALPHA live on testnet👇 pic.twitter.com/JiUDQUnuLt

Integrations

vDOT vaults are now live

vDOT vaults are now live on Interlay. vDOT asset can now be used as collateral for vaults. Vault operators no longer have to choose between L1 staking & bridge rewards & would be able to secure and earn from both.

A big step towards scaling the Trustless iBTC bridge via Liquid staking.

vDOT Lending and Borrowing Market Update

User can now Lend & Borrow vDOT and use vDOT as collateral to borrow iBTC, USDT and DOT on Interlay’s Bitcoin DeFi Hub.

October Community Call

Co-founder Alexei Zamyatin joined us for the Interlay Community Call to discuss our progress, new integrations, BOB & other important updates & future plans in our Bitcoin mission!

item.title: Announcing BOB: A new Bitcoin Layer-2 Stack
item.dc:creator: Interlay
item.content:encoded:
What is BOB?

BOB (“Build on Bitcoin”) a new Bitcoin layer 2 stack, featuring Rust smart contracts compatible with Bitcoin libraries such as Lightning and Ordinals. Combined with full support of the Ethereum Virtual Machine, BOB is the best place to innovate, experiment and build novel decentralized applications on top of Bitcoin’s stack.

Apart from Rust and EVM smart contracts, the first MVP of BOB already boasts a trustless BTC bridge and a built-in Bitcoin light client that cryptographically verifies the main chain, allowing teams to create trustless BTC, Ordinals and BRC swaps, as well as other BTC primitives such as hashrate markets.

Why BOB?

State of the industry

Bitcoin is experiencing a long-overdue renaissance. Our goal is to enable builders to create truly decentralized applications and innovate on top of Bitcoin’s existing stack, including Lightning, Ordinals and Nostr. BOB will be the catalyst for the Bitcoin building renaissance.

Our vision

Rollups are likely the best shot at ensuring long-term value accrual to Bitcoin, improving economic sustainability of the protocol even after future halving events and by extension, we consider ZK rollups currently being the best bet for such architecture, however we’re building BOB to support whatever cryptographic primitives find their way into Bitcoin.

BOB is a space for builders looking to innovate & build on Bitcoin with a view to democratise access to the advantages of the Bitcoin ecosystem & unlock novel use-cases. Bitcoin being the defensive layer for the entire Web3 ecosystem, BOB is here to not weaken it but to expand them in a focused direction & BOB is a manifestation of those efforts.

Builder Values

BOB encompasses a set of core values enabling builders to innovate on Bitcoin.

  • Experimentation: BOB will pioneer across all fields of bitcoin innovation & experimentation — Technology (rollups, ZK, AI, …), art (NFTs, …), Organization (DAOs), and Entertainment (social, …). BOB will never be closed off to specific areas but instead foster a diverse space of innovators.
  • Real-world impact: The innovations made must have an improvement for people by giving them access to Bitcoin values. BOB is an enabler to bring the BTC advantages to new and existing use cases.
  • Freedom of choice: Projects deployed on BOB should also be able to deploy on other rollups and chains. Builders should focus on the unique values of the product without having to worry about platform risk of BOB.

Early Alpha

BOB is just getting started with plenty of new things remaining to be built, researched, and experimented with. Our first MVP is out, and you can check out the early Alpha here https://docs.gobob.xyz/docs/build — and for a deeper dive, visit the newly launched BOB website at: https://www.gobob.xyz

Future roadmap

At BOB we’re developing novel ways to trustlessly bridge between Bitcoin, Ethereum, and the multi-chain ecosystem. Whether Bitcoin for DeFi, swapping Ordinals for USDC, or bringing decentralized stablecoins onto Lightning — BOB has got you covered, powered by cryptography and game theory.

The full-release schedule will introduce interoperability with Ethereum, trustless BTC peg protocols, and Bitcoin rollup mechanics.

Stay updated

If you’re interested in connecting with Bitcoin builders, don’t miss joining our Discord and heading straight to the BOB channels: https://discordapp.com/invite/interlay

Would you like to stay updated? Follow our official BOB Twitter: BOB | Build On Bitcoin

BOB Website: https://gobob.xyz
